answer: A violet dye marks each account's work history: every honest act tints the record a shade from the act itself, so one operator running many accounts leaves one dye across them, visible to all. To stay lit, each identity must tend a lantern at the wharf with steady verifiable service, checking answers and reporting faults, so presence needs ongoing effort, not a one-time payment. Standing ebbs like a tide: an idle identity dims and must re-earn it. Sybil clusters thus pay full honest-work cost for every copy, gaining nothing, since identical dye betrays them and dim lanterns drop out.
